lots.title: Provision of Asbestos Assessments
lots.description: Asbestos Specification for the London Borough of Bexley, contract commencement April 2026. Outlines Asbestos Surveys required to support the management of the Council's operational estate. Contract term 3 + 2 years. The Supplier shall provide all expertise, staff, labour, materials, equipment, and resources for the undertaking of Asbestos Surveys, working in collaboration with the Council's client team and other appointed suppliers. Services include management, refurbishment and demolition surveys, ad-hoc air monitoring, sampling services, re-inspection/monitoring, training, and specialist asbestos consultancy, all in accordance with the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 (enforced 2025) and HSE Guidance HSG264 (2025 update).
requirements: Provide all expertise, staff, labour, materials, equipment and resources to deliver Asbestos Surveys across the Council's operational estate (section 1 Introduction and Context).

Prepare an annual resource schedule of Asbestos Surveys aligned to Appendix B - Bexley Asbestos Surveys - Price Matrix, for Council approval; flag whether each activity is statutory compliance or best practice (section 2 General).
Keep doors, windows and lighting secure during surveys; maintain a key handover/return system with the Council FM Client Team and immediately report loss of keys (section 2 General).
Supplier must not move items of equipment or furniture (except for specialist maintenance) without Council agreement (section 2 General).

Deliver Asbestos Management Services including preparation of asbestos removal specifications and tender documents, vetting of method statements, and liaison with enforcement authorities (section 3 Specification of Services).
Provide Asbestos Consultancy Services managing contractors undertaking Project Works including supervision, control and planning (section 3 Specification of Services).
Manage planning, smoke test, removal, final clean / 4-stage clearance, and completion of asbestos works in accordance with the Plan of Work (section 4 Working Methods and Practices).

Ensure mandatory air monitoring in public buildings including schools and libraries, even for non-licensed work, and deliver ad-hoc air monitoring services (background, leak, reassurance, stage clearance, personal) (section 4 Working Methods and Practices).
Provide training for Council staff and suppliers on asbestos regulations, duties under the Control of Asbestos Regulations and related Codes of Practice (section 4 Working Methods and Practices).

Carry out Asbestos Surveys (Management, Refurbishment and Demolition) in accordance with HSE Guidance HSG264 (2025 update) across all internal/external areas and supplementary buildings (sheds, garages, stores) (section 5 Job Completion).

Provide plant and equipment for safe means of access including above 4m height (subject to prior written proposal and agreement); use suitable PPE/RPE (section 5 Job Completion - Asbestos Surveys General).
Perform Refurbishment Surveys (fully intrusive, destructive where necessary) with full sampling programme and volume/length/surface estimates of ACMs (section 5 Refurbishment Surveys).
Perform Demolition Surveys (fully intrusive, all buildings to be demolished) per HSG264 (2025 update) (section 5 Demolition Survey).

Perform Management Surveys locating ACMs that could be damaged during normal occupancy, including inspection of risers/loft areas, voids above suspended ceiling tiles, and all external areas (section 5 Management Surveys).
Perform Sampling Services where specific materials are sampled for analysis (section 5 Sampling Services).
Ensure all asbestos sampling is analysed by UKAS-accredited laboratories (ISO 17025) (sections 5, 6, 7).

Produce survey reports capturing Supplier identity, UKAS accreditation numbers, surveyor name, premises, dates, survey scope, methodology compliance with HSG264, deviations, inaccessible areas, negative results, and Material Assessment Algorithm scores per HSG264 (section 6 Documentation - Information to be Recorded).
Include Laboratory Analyst's Report (signed) within the Asbestos Report with site address, sample dates, reference numbers, results and material identification (section 6 Documentation).
Produce Material Assessment Algorithm and Priority Assessment scores; apply risk categories High/Medium/Low/Very Low per HSG264 (section 6 Documentation).
Conduct Priority Assessments in accordance with HSG227; carry out sampling in strict accordance with HSG264 (2025 update) and HSG248 (2022 amendment) (section 6 Documentation).

Comply with Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, statutory provisions, HSE guidance, and Disability Discrimination / Equalities legislation; submit RAMS approved by the Council before commencing work (section 7 Health and Safety Compliance).
Provide PPE, formally trained operatives, maintained training records submitted annually, and awareness of emergency evacuation procedures (section 7 Equipment and Training).
Presume ACMs in plant rooms and appliances unless proven otherwise; workplace risk assessments to be updated and available; cooperate on data protection (section 7 Risk Management).
Provide a single point of contact for Health and Safety matters; report all near misses and understand RIDDOR reporting obligations (section 7 Communication and Reporting).
Take two samples per surface for textured coatings (per HSG248 2022 amendment); do not clone presumption of ACMs between properties (section 7 Requirements).
Seal all sample points; paint over textured coating sample points; use UKAS-accredited ISO 17025 laboratory with full certificate included in report (section 7 Requirements).
Label obvious asbestos items lacking a label using industry-standard asbestos (a) labels during the survey (section 7 Labelling).
Access all areas including risers/voids using Mul-T-Lock and FB keys; liaise with site contacts to ensure access to restricted/no-access rooms on the day (section 7 Access).

Deliver annual re-inspection/monitoring of sites with ACMs: review floor plans, assess whole property, inspect known ACMs, sample previously presumed items, survey previously non-accessed areas, escalate damaged high-risk products (section 7 Re-inspections and Monitoring Service).

Work with Council-appointed FM, Lift, Fire Risk and Water Risk Supplier teams; no ACM disturbance without Council agreement; comply with Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 (enforced 2025) (section 7 Working with the Council and its contract partners).

Accept work via email and operate the Council's Asset Management / CAFM system Technology Forge (TF Cloud / Civica) for updates and invoicing; upload risk assessments in a CAFM-compatible format (section 8 Help Desk).

Invoice monthly via the Council's System (TF Cloud / Civica); email invoices to fmcu.buildingservices@bexley.gov.uk; all jobs on an invoice must be complete with documentation before payment; no recourse after invoicing (section 8 Invoicing).
Supplier to provide all equipment, tools and vehicles at own expense (section 9 Equipment, Tools & Vehicles).

Indemnify the Council against losses/injury; designate a Contract Manager; provide monthly/quarterly/annual performance, H&S and financial reports; attend monthly operational and quarterly partnership meetings (section 10 Contract Management).
Complete a Dynamic Risk Assessment prior to any planned or reactive works; perform Authorised Person duties; upload to CAFM as agreed (section 11 Permits to Work).
Adhere to Environmental Policy (Appendix C) and support the Council's Social Value objectives (section 25 referenced from section 11).

Detail organisation structure and escalation route during mobilisation; ensure staff competence, sickness/holiday cover, DBS checks (including sub-contractors), confidentiality agreements and site sign-in (section 12 Structure & Resourcing).

Use sub-contractors only with prior Council approval, following vetting and DBS checks; pass through performance measures contractually; implement KPI monitoring, spot-checks and regular management meetings (section 13 Sub-contractors).

Handle complaints: pass to FM Client Unit immediately; rectify failures within SLA; record and notify the Contract Administrator within 24 hours; provide monthly complaints schedule (sections 14 Complaints and 15 Customer Care).

During mobilisation: configure IT and reporting systems, agree report formats, meeting/reporting schedule, Asbestos Surveys programme of work and KPIs; present all initialisation documents at the mobilisation meeting (section 16 Mobilisation Work).
Propose new technologies and materials to drive continuous improvement, value for money, sustainability and health and safety (section 17 Continuous Improvement & Innovation).

warnings.message: Document is a single-lot specification ('6278 - Draft specification - Lot 3 - Provision of Asbestos Assessments'). Notice context at notice-level references 11 lots on Framework 6278; only Lot 3 is authoritatively described by this source document.

No CPV codes are cited within the tender specification body. Notice-level CPV codes (50700000-2, 50750000-7, 71315000-9) relate to the whole framework and are not evidence-anchored inside this Lot 3 specification, so cpv_codes is left empty rather than copied from notice metadata.

The document is a service specification, not an Invitation to Tender (ITT). Formal evaluation criteria with weightings are not present. Evaluation_criteria surfaces qualitative performance signals (KPIs, complaints reduction, social value, customer-care procedure) that the spec expects suppliers to evidence in their tender; weightings are unknown.

Source refers to the price schedule as both 'Appendix B - Bexley Asbestos Surveys - Price Matrix' (sections 2, 10) and 'Appendix 1 - Bexley Asbestos Surveys - Price Matrix' (section 8). Treated as the same referenced price matrix.
Docling markdown does not preserve explicit page numbers for this extraction (page_count=0 in document_extractions row). Evidence anchors use section headings instead of page numbers.

Source text restates 'Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 (enforced 2025)' and 'HSG264 (2025 update)' verbatim many times, including occasional doubled '(2025 update) (2025 update)' strings indicating a template find-replace; treated as the single authoritative reference.

London Borough of Bexley

Asbestos Specification

Contract Commencement

April 2026
This Service Specification provides an outline of Asbestos Surveys that are required to support the management of the Council's operational estate.
The contract will be for a period of 3 + 2 years.
Appendix B - Bexley Asbestos Surveys - Price Matrix
The Council require the following Asbestos Surveying Services set out below to ensure compliance with the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 (enforced 2025) and HSE Guidance HSG264 (2025 update)
Asbestos Management Services - Preparation of Specifications and Tender documents
Asbestos Consultancy Services - Managing contractors undertaking Project Works including Supervision, Control and Planning
Mandatory air monitoring is required in public buildings including schools and libraries, even for non-licensed work.
The ability to train Council staff and Suppliers
Asbestos Surveys are to be carried out in accordance with HSE Guidance HSG264 (2025 update)
A Refurbishment Survey will be required before any refurbishment or demolition works are carried out.
This survey is required prior to the demolition of a building and is fully intrusive into the fabric of all the buildings to be demolished.
A management survey is a standard survey. Its purpose is to locate, as far as reasonably practicable, the presence and extent of any suspect ACMs in the building
This is an exercise where it is required to collect a sample from a material and location specified by the council.
Sampling to be carried out in strict accordance with HSG264 (2025 update) (2025 update) and HSG248 (2022 amendment)
Priority Assessments where required must be conducted according to HSG 227.
A risk category shall be assigned to each asbestos containing material based on the categorisation and overall scores within HSG264 (2025 update) (2025 update), i.e. High, Medium, Low and Very Low.
